outcome: No progress on the existence question since 26 January 2024: no Wall–Sun–Sun prime has been found, none has been ruled out by proof, and the computational search bound (2^64, established by PrimeGrid's Wieferich and Wall-Sun-Sun Prime Search project, which concluded in December 2022) predates the window and has not been reported extended since.
summary: The existence of Wall–Sun–Sun primes (equivalently Fibonacci–Wieferich primes) remains open: none is known, and it is conjectured (not proved) that infinitely many exist. The only substantive activity in the record is PrimeGrid's 'Wieferich and Wall-Sun-Sun Prime Search' distributed-computing project, which extended the search bound to 2^64 (≈1.8×10^19) before concluding in December 2022 — this predates the 26 January 2024 frozen revision date and is therefore not a change within the window; per §3.1, an infinitude/existence question of this type is not advanced merely by extending a search bound in any case, since the bound is not itself the question asked. I found no report of PrimeGrid or anyone else extending the search further after 2022, and no new theoretical result bearing on the existence question itself. Two arXiv papers turned up in searches — 'A new condition for k-Wall-Sun-Sun primes' (2023-02, predates window regardless) and 'The p-adic Valuations of Möbius Duals of Lucas Sequences' (Ross, Shen, Cai, arXiv:2512.03481, December 2025) — but both concern generalized/variant notions (k-Wall-Sun-Sun primes, a different Lucas-sequence-based construction) rather than the classical Wall–Sun–Sun primes as stated in the bullet; per §3.1 these are related problems, not cases of this one, so they do not count as movement on this bullet. No AI involvement of any kind was found in connection with this problem — the searching and the theoretical papers are entirely conventional distributed computing and human mathematics. This is a clean 'nothing happened' record.
competing_reading: One could argue the k-Wall-Sun-Sun and Möbius-dual papers are close enough in spirit (they generalize the same congruence condition) that a reader might want them mentioned even though they don't count as progress on the stated existence question; I've noted them above but excluded them from the status per the case-vs-variant rule, since they change the object of study (introducing a parameter k, or a different dual construction) rather than restricting the original question.
what_would_settle_it: A published proof or disproof of existence, or (short of that) a credible report that PrimeGrid or another group has extended the search bound beyond 2^64 with a written announcement dated after 26 January 2024 — though per §3.1 even such an extension would not change the status of this existence question, only narrow where an answer could hide.
